status_notes: Source-level entries only. Item-level identifiers (objectives, tables, annexes) not yet researched.
notes: RTCA, Inc. is a US private, not-for-profit association that develops consensus-based technical guidance for aviation, published as DO-series documents and adopted by the FAA through Technical Standard Orders and Advisory Circulars. EUROCAE is its European counterpart; most DO documents have a paired ED document with equivalent content. Documents are paywalled.

match_nodes.description: DO-178C — Software Considerations in Airborne Systems and Equipment Certification

data.notes: The airborne software assurance standard. Objectives are scoped by software level A-E, derived from failure-condition severity via the ARP4761 safety assessment. Supplements: DO-330 (tool qualification), DO-331 (model-based development), DO-332 (object-oriented technology), DO-333 (formal methods). Paired with EUROCAE ED-12C.

match_nodes.description: DO-254 — Design Assurance Guidance for Airborne Electronic Hardware

data.notes: The hardware counterpart to DO-178C, covering complex custom micro-coded components such as ASICs and FPGAs. Uses hardware design assurance levels A-E on the same failure-condition basis.

The airworthiness **security** standard — explicitly cybersecurity rather than functional safety. Establishes the Airworthiness Security Process for showing that intentional unauthorised electronic interaction does not adversely affect airworthiness. Companions: DO-356A / ED-203A (security methods and considerations) and DO-355 / ED-204 (continuing airworthiness security in service). Paired with EUROCAE ED-202A.

match_nodes.description: DO-356A — Airworthiness Security Methods and Considerations

data.notes: Methods and techniques supporting the DO-326A process: security risk assessment, threat identification, and security-measure effectiveness. Paired with EUROCAE ED-203A.

match_nodes.description: DO-355 — Information Security Guidance for Continuing Airworthiness

data.notes: Covers information security for aircraft already in service — the continuing-airworthiness half of the DO-326A family, including operator and maintainer responsibilities. Paired with EUROCAE ED-204.
